 Micron: A $150 Billion AI Reckoning Is Coming
 Nov 03, 2026, 10:05 AM ET Micron Technology, Inc. (MU) Stock , ZMIC:CA Stock , MU:CA Stock SOX , DRAM , GOOG , GOOGL , MSFT , AMZN , META , KXIAY , KXHCF , SSNLF , SKHY , ZGOO:CA , ZAMZ:CA , ZMET:CA , SSNHZ , ZMSF:CA , MTPDL , MSFT:CA , META:CA , GOOG:CA , AMZN:CA 31 Comments 1 Like Summit Research 13.1K Followers Follow Summary
 Micron Technology, Inc. has led the recent memory sector selloff despite record fiscal Q4 earnings and improving long-term demand visibility.
 Tightening credit conditions and mounting hyperscaler financing pressures are intensifying scrutiny over the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending and memory pricing momentum.
 The concern has been amplified by Japanese peer Kioxia's tepid earnings outlook, which suggests an emerging moderation in memory and storage demand and pricing.
 However, MU's increasing take-or-pay volumes and expanding pricing protections under SCAs reinforce earnings resilience against historical cyclical pressures, supporting prospects for valuation recovery.
 In the following analysis, I discuss risks facing MU's outlook and whether its strategic shift to long-term supply agreements can sustain margin and ROI durability amid mounting infrastructure spending headwinds.
 JHVEPhoto/iStock Editorial via Getty Images
 Memory stocks have led the broader AI-driven market selloff over the past month. The weakness reflects renewed investor concerns over the durability of elevated AI infrastructure spending commitments and their growing reliance on debt financing
